items.Sentence: Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • A membrane filtration influent tank;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • A surge tank and supporting compressed air system to control pressure surges;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • A feed pump system to convey influent from the influent tank to the microfiltration/ultrafiltration (MF/UF) system;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • A MF/UF membrane filtration system with associated chemical addition, backwash, and chemical cleaning and membrane conditioning processes;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • An inter-process storage tank to equalize flows between the MF/UF and reverse osmosis (RO) systems;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • RO transfer pumps and cartridge filters to convey MF/UF filtrate from the inter-process storage tank to the RO feed pumps;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • A RO feed pump station;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • RO treatment trains with associated chemical addition, backwash, chemical cleaning, and membrane conditioning processes;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • A product water blending and storage tank;
Key components of the MFRO Facility will include: • A pump system to convey blended MFRO product water to agricultural reuse sites via Hogback Reservoir.
The following MFRO waste or residuals streams will be discharged to a 15-inch-diameter brine pipeline for conveyance to the ELO and SEOO: • MF/UF backwash flows,

The following MFRO waste or residuals streams will be discharged to a 15-inch-diameter brine pipeline for conveyance to the ELO and SEOO: • RO concentrate (brine), and • Periodic RO “clean in place” membrane cleaning and conditioning flows.

The following low-flow MFRO waste or residuals streams will be discharged to an on-site waste equalization wet well prior to discharge to the sanitary sewer for treatment at HARRF: • Periodic MF/UF neutralized “clean in place” membrane cleaning and conditioning flows,
